claims.text: The proposed framework combines ML-refined, DFT-based interatomic potentials with separate phonon and electron Boltzmann transport calculations.
The framework will predict lattice and electronic thermal conductivity in HfNbTaTiZr independently.
The framework will improve predictive accuracy by approximately 30% relative to previous methods.
The target material is concentrated, nearly defect-free bulk HfNbTaTiZr.
High-temperature HfNbTaTiZr specimens have been observed with approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
The phonon calculation incorporates temperature-dependent anharmonicity and defect or impurity effects.
The framework is applicable below 200 K.
Lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions in HfNbTaTiZr are comparable below 200 K.
The framework is applicable from 300 to 1200 K for oxygen-containing specimens.
Local variations in atomic masses, force constants, and oxygen content are structural mediators of heat transport in HfNbTaTiZr.
Anharmonic phonon calculations provide the lattice thermal-conductivity contribution.
Electron Boltzmann transport calculations using refined DFT inputs provide the electronic thermal-conductivity contribution.
Separating the phonon and electron channels avoids assumptions involving a fixed Debye temperature and perfect crystals.
Earlier HEA computational approaches are limited by inadequate force fields or simplified representations of atomic-scale complexity.
Previous approaches conflate lattice and electronic heat transport.
For oxygen-containing HfNbTaTiZr at high temperatures, the predicted total conductivity will lie within 10–17 W/(K·m).
The approach is valid only for nearly defect-free samples or variants containing approximately 1 wt.% oxygen and is uncertain above 1200 K or for substantially more defective samples.
Time-domain thermoreflectance or laser-flash analysis can provide a separately measured lattice thermal conductivity for the proposed comparison.
Concurrent electrical measurements and the Wiedemann–Franz law can estimate the electronic thermal-conductivity contribution where applicable.
The exact accuracy improvement is uncertain because of ML-potential training and impurity-modeling uncertainties.

contradictions.description: The conditions specify applicability only below 200 K and from 300 to 1200 K, whereas the boundary describes validity throughout 0–1200 K, implicitly including the otherwise unspecified 200–300 K interval.

The central claim is a 30% relative accuracy improvement over prior methods, but the falsification rule instead uses a 30% absolute prediction-error margin and does not require a 30% improvement relative to the baseline.
